title: Strengthening Regulatory Regime for Nursing Homes
what_it_is: Strengthening Regulatory Regime for Nursing Homes

sections.label: MOH nursing home regulatory oversight
sections.summary: MOH conducts audits, reviews and inspections of nursing homes, and escalates measures when gaps are serious and repeated, as in two licence revocations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health): Sir, as part of the Ministry of Health's (MOH's) regulatory oversight over providers, we conduct regular and periodic audits, special thematic reviews and inspections on nursing homes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: This includes off-cycle audits in response to feedback and complaints to ensure residents' safety.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: The great majority of nursing homes placed on closer monitoring take adequate corrective actions and sustain the improvements.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: However, if the gaps are serious, repeated and there is a lack of serious effort to rectify them, such as in the case of Windsor Convalescent Home and LC Nursing Home, MOH will have to escalate our measures.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: These two cases of licence revocation are therefore an outcome of the regulatory framework working as intended.

sections.label: Licence revocation and Vanguard Healthcare
sections.summary: When remediation efforts were inadequate or not sustained for two operators, MOH revoked their licences and arranged for Vanguard Healthcare to step in.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: When we ascertained that the remediation efforts were inadequate or were not sustained for the two operators, we revoked their licences and arranged for Vanguard Healthcare to step in.

sections.label: MOH takeover and private claims
sections.summary: MOH may take over operations or coordinate resident relocation, but cannot coordinate private claims against nursing homes as care is a contract.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: When necessary, we will step in and take over the operations or coordinate the relocation of residents to another facility.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: However, as the provision of care is a contract between the resident and the nursing home, MOH is unable to coordinate private claims from residents or their families against the nursing home.

sections.label: Support for nursing homes
sections.summary: MOH supports nursing homes through manpower training grants and other support, raising collective standards of care and professionalism across the sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: To his point about supporting nursing homes, we do support our nursing homes through different support from manpower training grants to other support for nursing homes, raising the collective standard of care and professionalism across the whole nursing home sector.

sections.label: Information for caregivers and families
sections.summary: MOH is continually looking at how to provide meaningful information for caregivers and family members to make a decision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: MOH is continually looking at how we can provide meaningful information for caregivers and family members to make a decision.
